machine.description: Soulmate is an easy difficulty Linux machine featuring a multi-stage exploitation chain. An HTTP server hosts CrushFTP 11, which is vulnerable to CVE-2025-31161 authentication bypass. After creating an admin user, the attacker resets a privileged FTP user's password, uploads a reverse shell, and gains initial foothold. Local enumeration reveals a restricted SSH ForceCommand wrapper and an internal Erlang/OTP SSH service on 127.0.0.1:2222. Port forwarding exposes the service, which is exploited for root access.

sections.title: Phase 1 — Reconnaissance
sections.content: Discover open ports (22 SSH, 80 HTTP). HTTP redirects to soulmate.htb domain. Virtual host fuzzing reveals ftp.soulmate.htb.

sections.title: Phase 2 — Application Enumeration
sections.content: CrushFTP 11 login panel found. Version fingerprinted as March 2025 build. CVE-2025-31161 identified as authentication bypass vulnerability.

sections.title: Phase 3 — CVE Exploitation (Auth Bypass)
sections.content: CVE-2025-31161: CrushFTP auth bypass via crafted HTTP header. Creates admin user with arbitrary credentials.

sections.title: Phase 4 — Privilege Abuse (Admin Panel)
sections.content: Use admin access to reset password of user with FTP write access. Upload webshell/reverse shell via FTP to web-accessible directory.

sections.title: Phase 5 — Remote Code Execution
sections.content: Trigger uploaded reverse shell. Obtain shell as www-data.

sections.title: Phase 6 — Local Enumeration
sections.content: Run linpeas. Discover SSH ForceCommand wrapper for user ben. Find Erlang SSH service on 127.0.0.1:2222. Discover hardcoded credentials.

sections.title: Phase 7 — Port Forwarding
sections.content: Forward internal Erlang SSH port to attacker machine.

sections.title: Phase 8 — Root Exploitation
sections.content: Exploit Erlang/OTP SSH RCE via port-forwarded service. Obtain root shell.

kill_chain: RCE: reverse shell via uploaded file
key_lessons: Multi-stage chains require stateful credential tracking
